input.command: grep -n -i "overdue\|due\|Date\|todo-logic" index.html | head -60; ls check 2>/dev/null; grep -rn "timezone\|UTC\|local" --include=*.md . 2>/dev/null | head
input.description: Find due-date usage in index.html and project notes
Check how today is computed and test in LA timezone
Test overdue logic across the day in LA timezone

content.text:
I couldn't reproduce this, so I didn't change any code.

- **Project rule:** a due date is saved as a plain `YYYY-MM-DD` date in the user's own time zone and never converted to UTC. A task is overdue only when its due date is before today.
- **The code follows it:** `todo-logic.js:41-49` builds "today" from the local date and compares plain date strings. `index.html:118,220` uses the same values.
- **Test:** I ran the logic in California time with a task due 2026-09-13, at 8am, 4pm, 5pm, 8pm and 11pm. In UTC those later times are already the next day. The task was never marked overdue.

Chose: no fix, because the report can't be reproduced under the local-date rule.
Rejected: digging further or changing the date logic, since the code already follows the rule.
